graph.title: Christmas Train
notes: INTENTIONALLY TWO SEPARATE GROUPS (validator L3): the booklet builds two separate models. The first is the three-car train (loco, tender, coach, pages 3-62); the second is the free-standing tree and lamp-flag scene (pages 63-68). Page 69 shows them side by side, and no instruction joins or attaches them. So the tree scene (b148-b163) is deliberately not connected to the train.
Inside the train, the three vehicles are joined with a clip-and-knob coupling: loco b9 to tender b70, tender b65 to coach b115.

Piece ids come from the inventory page (page 70/71). Element IDs there are 6–7 digits; colours were read from the pictures. b164 is the second red 1x1 plate (302421, 2x on inventory; loco step 3 shows 2x). It was added after the original numbering, so it is out of build order.

Where the catalogue has no entry I added new types. These include the 2x4 mudguard plates, spoked wheel, window frame and glass, boiler parts, dark green plates and slopes, pearl-gold fences and handle plates, and the tree. The knob on the 1x4 plate (lego-4516020) is modelled as a bar port so the clip-on-bar coupling is a compatible pair. lego-346021 (1x8 plate) has stud.1-stud.8 so each post and window gets its own stud.

lego-614126 is the black 1x1 round plate used as a buffer here. The catalogue describes that id as a small wheel, but I used it because the inventory id matches. lego-4541191 is the grille slope on the loco front.

Wheel holders sit on the studs of the upside-down mudguards (steps 5, 11, 16), so each holder joins the mudguard's stud port. Tender posts use the top.1/top.2 ports of the 1x6 red plates (catalogue lego-366621). Loco posts use b37 stud.1/stud.2 and the loco window frame uses b37 stud.3.

Several sub-steps show an assembly floating or flipped. Exactly which stud each piece sits on is inferred from the isometric pictures, so many joins are approximate. Examples: gold handle plates and 1x1 plates, the cargo stacks and cookies on the tender, and the coach fences and bricks. Most edges name no port.
The orange and lime 3-piece cargo stacks on the tender (plate, black 1x1 plate, tile) are both modelled, but the booklet only clearly shows the lime one placed.
The two gold rods sit in the clip plates on the loco sides (two clips per rod, assumed). The gold handle plates are separate pieces.

Wheelsets are 7 repeats of a 2x2 wheel holder plus two wheels (3 loco, 2 tender, 2 coach, 14 wheels). Window units are 6 repeats of frame plus glass (2 loco, 4 coach). Round-plate stacks (posts) are repeats: 2 on the loco, 4 on the tender and 4 on the coach. Loco and coach posts end in a white round brick; tender posts end in gold.
The tender candy-cane tower is built as a stack, bottom to top: red, green, white, red, green, white round plates, then the red curved brick, then a red tile.
